_about: The gaps the gauntlet asserts. Each row is one component, the verified vault file it is held
against, the figure read off that file's frames in vault/SPECS.md, and a measurement of the
app's own specimen that has to come out the same way.
A row without `assert` is honest about being a caution or a counter-example: the sheet shows
it, the run prints it, and nobody is allowed to call it a pass.
test/gauntlet.test.mjs refuses a row naming a file the eye never verified, a component that
is not in the registry, or a figure that is not the one SPECS.md measured.
A row carries `referenceRelation`. `informs` means the record is in this component's own for-list in
vault/SPECS-FOR.json -- the picture informs the drawing -- and `test/gauntlet.test.mjs` refuses the
row otherwise. `origin` means the picture is where the DEMAND was first measured, and makes no claim
that it informs this drawing; such a row carries `originClaim` saying how it entered, and it is never
coverage for the component. The distinction exists because de-quoting a component from a record has to
be allowed to coexist with a row that was honestly born from reading that record.

gaps.notHeld: Two facts, and one of them changed since this row was written. `tape` is the DECISION tape — a queue of waits with an `elapsed` clock per row and no axis to cross, so it was never the place for a marker. The axis objection used to run against `river` too: every lane normalised its own first and last stamp across the plate, so no two lanes agreed on where now is. That is gone — `river` now derives one span from every lane's events, draws one ruler and one now-line with a clamped x and its stamp beside it (src/components/river.js, test/river-axis.test.mjs). What still stops the sweep is not geometry but honesty, and the component says so in its own comment: the ruler and the now-line are furniture, furniture carries no mark, and a playhead translating left to right across a deck would move on nothing — there is no sample clock in the fixture, so a sweeping line would be the exact motion the honesty rack exists to catch. The audio editor gets away with it because playback position is a measured quantity against a real clock. Until a source declares one, the reference is quoted for the idiom it does support — named tracks, one ruler across the whole plate, ground before the first event drawn as ground — and the sweep stays unbuilt.

A dispatch panel that animates its own furniture on every refresh says 'everything changed' when one row did, so the furniture must hold still over a change.

Correcting the reading matters here: demanding an untouched legend from a component with no legend would be the `mfd` mistake in a new costume.
